label: L11 · Resistance & Stewardship
rows: Drivers of resistance
Agricultural overuse (plants, animals) · inappropriate prescribing → STEWARDSHIP (clinician + patient education) · prophylaxis · patient NON-COMPLIANCE.
Resistance
The antibiotic can no longer kill or control the bacteria — a property of the BUG, not a patient allergy.
Stewardship cycle
DIAGNOSE bacterial disease → consider a NON-ANTIBIOTIC alternative → use antimicrobials JUDICIOUSLY when needed → RE-EVALUATE the need.
Six facts
Life-saving · bacterial infections ONLY · some ear infections and MOST sore throats need none · green mucus ≠ antibiotic · every drug has risks (allergy, rash, diarrhea).
Resistance follows use
Over 100 antibiotics on the market; penicillin, vancomycin, azithromycin each met resistance within years of widespread use.
Superbugs

MRSA/MSSA · VRSA/VISA · toxigenic Escherichia coli · Clostridioides difficile · Neisseria gonorrhoeae · Mycobacterium tuberculosis · carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella · vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus · Pseudomonas. ESKAPE pathogens top the NOSOCOMIAL lists.

label: L11 · Choosing Antibiotics Today
rows: Disk diffusion (Kirby-Bauer)
Antibiotic paper disks on inoculated agar → ZONE OF INHIBITION = drug stopped growth. Growth up to the disk = little effect.
Antibiogram
Susceptibility PERCENTAGES by organism and drug → guides EMPIRIC therapy. Vancomycin covered both MSSA and MRSA on the example.
Antibiogram limits
No minimum inhibitory concentration · no patient risk factors · no synergy data · may be ONE hospital only.
Empiric therapy
Started BEFORE cultures/results · critically ill or emergent · based on experience + antibiograms · then ADJUSTED (e.g. intravenous → oral). Not the same as prophylaxis.

label: L11 · Prophylaxis & Adverse Effects
rows: When prophylaxis

Prosthetic devices (BIOFILM) · before surgery (surgical site infection) · immunocompromised (human immunodeficiency virus, chemotherapy, transplant) · CONTACTS of tuberculosis, meningitis, pertussis · dental work only for a few high-risk (prosthetic valve, prior endocarditis) · animal bites, penetrating brain injury.
Direct adverse effects
Allergy (even life-threatening) · kidney/liver toxicity · drug-drug interactions · therapeutic failure.
Indirect adverse effects
Commensal flora damage → Clostridioides difficile · resistant infection · ENVIRONMENTAL flora (antibiotics in food and water).

label: L11 · Fecal Transplant & Phage Therapy
rows: Fecal microbiota transplant
Screened DONOR STOOL restores the gut flora · centuries old (“yellow soup”) · researched for Clostridioides difficile; recurrent infection is its established use.
Routes and safety

Nasogastric tube · colonoscopy · enema (recording adds frozen oral capsules) · STOOL BANKS · donor screening like BLOOD BANKS: human immunodeficiency virus, hepatitis A/B/C, syphilis, Clostridioides difficile, Giardia, Cryptosporidium. Vets: “transfaunation”.
Bacteriophages
Viruses that attack ONLY bacteria · DNA or RNA, never both · lytic or lysogenic · therapy needs LYTIC phages · head holds the genome; tail, baseplate, tail fibers attach and inject.
Phage pros
Multidrug-resistant targets · NARROW spectrum spares the microbiome · low side effects · wide distribution · less inflammation · maybe cheaper · die off with their host.
Phage cons

Dose/route/frequency/duration undefined · MUST know the causative agent (slow, costly) · gene transfer to the host bacterium · insurance · no phage product approved as a medicine yet → investigational drug status, emergency use authorization. Abandoned in the West when antibiotics arrived.

label: L11 · Other Alternatives
rows: Host-directed
Systemic CORTICOSTEROIDS ↓ inflammation (no killing) · intravenous immunoglobulin G and CONVALESCENT plasma (antibodies from recovered donors).
Prebiotic vs probiotic
PREbiotic = fiber that feeds the flora · PROBIOTIC = the live organism: Lactobacillus (bacterium), Saccharomyces (fungus), in FERMENTED foods.
Diet
The more diverse your PLANT intake, the more diverse your gut microbiota (American Gut project).
Plant essential oils
Antibacterial IN VITRO; better experimental design needed. Spice use predicted heaviest in HOT climates with rapid food spoilage.
